## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [15. August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.158
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.158
- Datum: 15.8.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hanna & Manfred,

Friday, Aug 15th 41
It is a few hours before sailing
time and we shall both be glad to get under way,
although I am a little worried about sea-sickness because
it is rainy and windy to-day. This is, however of minor im-
portance and the main aim is to get settled down there
as quickly as possible. We went to Boston last night to
see Eva, and we tortured her by bringing parcels to Mrs.
Sch. (Your books and birthday letters are all there and
waiting for the birthday). But she had a treat in various
ways. First we went over to let Stefan have a glimpse of
the new Amity Mall. Then - already past bedtime - Fullepo
took us over to Ossining to say goodbye to Mrs. Zweig N°1,
Eva went with us, and in addition to that attraction was
taken to a bar and treated to a coca-cola and ice cream
- at 9.30 p.m.! So I hope she will always remember that
there is something nice in our leaving and not mind too
much. - Her slightly high-brow letter style is, I believe, her
own; and maybe it can be traced back to Manfred, maybe
it is just the sign of an effort to write well. On the whole I
would call the surroundings more child-like than highbrow,
although with an intellectual tendency for those only who
are inclined that way, and since my own childhood I
have not seen children who managed to get themselves
so dirty in the garden than there. But they all get clean
again in the bath at night and Eva and Marion etc,
the big girls, even wash their own dresses because
the laundry is not very good. Even I, who do certainly
not belong to the washing sort of women, have got so far.
You would never believe what a laundry can do to your
things, they even managed to turn Eva's Bath school dresses
from blue into a pretty pale green! Well this is America
and Rio is not much better on the whole. They wash better,
because machines would be too expensive, but they cannot
yet dry-clean. Again, there are minor matters in a mad world
like ours.
L.T.Z.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf zwei Seiten (hier Seite 1). Tinte violett. Die Unterschrift 'L.T.Z.' steht für Lotte Zweig.

pages.transcription:
We were sorry to hear that Manfred's holiday
is already over, and you did not mention whether he
already got a job in his new capacity as Xray specialist.
I can understand that you do not want to live in a
flat for always, and I think the idea of taking a
house is on the whole very good. I am sure Wooster
or Frost would help you with the first cash payment,
but we both think it would only be worth while if you
can get a mortgage on the rest - from a bank or corporation
as it used to be done - and pay them the interest as
rent. Besides this of course only a buying in your joint
names is to be considered. Any other arrangement could
complicate matters one day. I remember those houses
in Ingram Avenue very well and also similar, but
smaller ones in St. Johns Wood. - With regard to the friends
you mention I it seems that you mostly associate with
yours now and neglect your own. But maybe this is only be-
cause you tell us only about ours. I would like to know,
however, what became of all the others, doctors, Joss etc. -
I got a little album for the photos you sent me and this,
too, is awaiting Eva's birthday. Mrs. Sch. was still considering
yesterday which special treat for Eva's group would be the
best to celebrate the event. - I wonder how Marta will
feel on her "visit" to Rosemount. Tell her she must write me
about it. - What you write about "Fantasia" was our impression
too. We left after the first part feeling quite dizzy. Besides
that and some very old Chaplin films we have seen nothing. But
on the boat we will have, I hope, a few good new films.
Well this is all for today and the last letter from USA,
at least for a while. It was a difficult decision to take,
and I had to think so hard as never in my life. I never
missed you as much - though I always miss you - than in
these weeks.
Best love to you all
Lotte.
